questions.scenario: An app at 10.20.10.8 connects to RDS at 10.20.21.18 in the same 10.20.0.0/16 VPC. The app route table also has 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway. Which route wins?

options.text: A public internet gateway route.
No route because the subnets differ.

questions.explanation: The local route is more specific than the default route and carries traffic between VPC subnets. Learn more in [VPC route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html).

questions.scenario: A subnet has 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, but an EC2 instance has only a private IPv4 address. Can the instance initiate IPv4 internet traffic directly through the IGW?

options.text: Yes, the route automatically creates a public address.
No, it also needs a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP.
No, internet gateways support inbound traffic only.
Yes, if its security group has no rules.

questions.explanation: An IGW route does not assign a public address. Public IPv4 communication also requires a public IPv4 or Elastic IP. Learn more in [VPC route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html).

questions.scenario: Private app subnets in two AZs use one NAT gateway in us-east-1a. What operational concern should the design review surface?

options.text: NAT gateways accept inbound internet connections.
NAT gateways replace security groups.
An AZ failure or cross-AZ path can affect private outbound traffic, so per-AZ NAT paths may better match the resilience target.
NAT gateways route local VPC traffic.

questions.explanation: A NAT gateway is zonal. Route design should match the required failure boundary and account for cross-AZ traffic. Learn more in [NAT gateway basics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html).

questions.scenario: A private subnet has 0.0.0.0/0 to NAT and a managed S3 prefix-list route to a gateway endpoint. Where should S3 traffic go?

options.text: NAT because default routes always win.
The internet gateway attached to the VPC.
The local route because S3 is in the same account.
The gateway endpoint because its destination is more specific.

questions.explanation: Longest-prefix matching selects the managed prefix-list endpoint route over the default NAT route. Learn more in [VPC route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html).

questions.scenario: A private task cannot download a package from the internet. Which checks directly test the outbound route path?

options.text: The subnet association points to the expected route table.
The Route 53 hosted zone has an MX record.
The route table has a usable 0.0.0.0/0 target.
Change the public hosted-zone TTL before inspecting the packet path.
The NAT gateway is available in a public subnet with an IGW route.

questions.explanation: The path depends on association, default route, NAT state and placement, and the NAT subnet path to the IGW. Learn more in [NAT gateway troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html).
